record.paper_title: Norming Markushevich bases: recent results and open problems
record.original_question: Does every weakly compactly generated Banach space admit a norming Markushevich basis? Here “weakly compactly generated” means that the space has a weakly compact subset whose linear span is dense, and a “norming Markushevich basis” means a fundamental total biorthogonal system whose biorthogonal functionals span a norming subspace of the dual.

evidence.quote: Problem 4.1 (John–Zizler). Does every WCG Banach space admit a norming M-basis?
Both these problems have been recently solved in the negative [50, 53] and we shall give more details on this in Section 4.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a Banach space with dual $X^*$. A biorthogonal system $\{(x_\alpha, x_\alpha^*) : \alpha \in \Lambda\} \subseteq X \times X^*$ (so that $x_\beta^*(x_\alpha) = \delta_{\alpha\beta}$) is called a Markushevich basis (M-basis) of $X$ if:
(i) $\overline{\mathrm{span}}\{x_\alpha : \alpha \in \Lambda\} = X$ (fundamental), and
(ii) $\{x_\alpha^* : \alpha \in \Lambda\}$ separates the points of $X$ (total).

The M-basis is called norming if the closed linear subspace $\overline{\mathrm{span}}^{\,w^*}\{x_\alpha^* : \alpha \in \Lambda\} \subseteq X^*$ is a norming subspace of $X^*$, i.e., there exists a constant $c > 0$ such that
$$\|x\| \le \frac{1}{c}\sup\{|f(x)| : f \in \overline{\mathrm{span}}\{x_\alpha^*\},\ \|f\| \le 1\} \quad \text{for all } x \in X.$$

A Banach space $X$ is called weakly compactly generated (WCG) if there exists a weakly compact subset $K \subseteq X$ such that $\overline{\mathrm{span}}\, K = X$.

Question: Does every weakly compactly generated Banach space admit a norming Markushevich basis?
artifact.status_search_result: The John–Zizler problem has been solved in the negative. Hájek, Todorčević and others constructed a Hilbert generated (hence WCG) Banach space that does not admit any norming M-basis (published in Advances in Mathematics, 2019). A further example by Russo (Mathematika, 2023) shows that even some $C(K)$ spaces that are WCG fail to have a norming M-basis.

status_evidence.title: Hilbert generated Banach spaces need not have a norming Markushevich basis
status_evidence.snippet: A Hilbert generated Banach space is constructed which admits no norming Markushevich basis, solving a classical problem of John and Zizler.
status_evidence.claim: WCG (even Hilbert generated) spaces need not admit norming M-bases; John–Zizler problem solved in the negative.

status_evidence.title: Banach spaces of continuous functions without norming Markushevich bases
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of WCG C(K) spaces with no norming M-basis.
status_evidence.claim: Additional negative solutions to the John–Zizler problem within C(K) spaces.
